pos.zh: 鸭；鸭肉
低头躲闪；迅速弯身；潜入水中

senses.title: A water bird
senses.definition: a common bird with a flat bill that swims on water
senses.definitionCN: 一种扁嘴、常在水面游动的鸟
senses.example: A mother duck led six ducklings across the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭妈妈带着六只小鸭游过湖面。
senses.why: The bird is the oldest and simplest image of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟是这个词最古老、最直接的画面。

senses.title: The meat as food
senses.definition: the meat of a duck eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物的鸭肉
senses.example: They ordered half a roast duck for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们点了半只烤鸭当晚餐。
senses.why: The animal's name names the meat on the table.
senses.whyCN: 动物的名字被用来命名餐桌上的肉。

senses.title: Lower the head quickly
senses.definition: to bend the head or body down quickly to avoid being hit or seen
senses.definitionCN: 迅速低头或弯身，以避免被打中或被发现
senses.example: He ducked under the low branch.
senses.exampleCN: 他低头躲过低垂的树枝。
senses.why: The bird plunges its head under water; a person plunges the head down the same way.
senses.whyCN: 鸭子把头扎进水里，人也以同样的方式猛地低头。

senses.title: Dive quickly into water
senses.definition: to go under the surface of water for a moment
senses.definitionCN: 短暂潜入水面之下
senses.example: The boy ducked under the waves to cool down.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩潜入浪下让自己凉快一下。
senses.why: The same plunging motion moved from bird to swimmer.
senses.whyCN: 同一个扎水的动作从鸟转移到游泳的人。

intro.en: Duck is a plain Germanic bird word whose verb sense grew from the bird's plunging habit.
intro.cn: duck 是一个朴素的日耳曼水鸟词，动词义从鸟扎水的习性中长出。

items.en: Old English duce meant a diver, a duck that plunges under water.
items.cn: 古英语 duce 意为「潜水者」，指会扎进水里的鸭。

items.en: It came from a Germanic root *dukan, to bend or duck down.
items.cn: 它源自日耳曼词根 *dukan，意为弯下、低头。

items.en: Middle English kept both the bird and the verb duck, to plunge or lower the head.
items.cn: 中古英语同时保留了名词「鸭」与动词 duck「扎水、低头」。

items.en: In cooking and markets the word also covered the meat of the bird.
items.cn: 在烹饪与市场中，这个词也涵盖鸭肉。

items.en: Modern English added a sitting duck for an easy target and ducky for fine or excellent.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了 a sitting duck（易受攻击的目标）与 ducky（好极了）等用法。

note.en: These words stand near duck in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 duck 相邻。

entries.definition: to go head first into water

normalIntro.en: Use the flat-bill plunging bird and the duck family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「扁嘴扎水」的鸭子和 duck 词族来记。

normal.en: duck the bird and duck your head share one plunging motion.
normal.cn: 「鸭子」与「低头躲闪」共用同一个扎水动作。

normal.en: duckling is a small duck, thanks to the -ling ending.
normal.cn: duckling 是小鸭子，多亏 -ling 这个小后缀。

normal.en: roast duck is the bird on the dinner table.
normal.cn: roast duck 就是端上餐桌的那只鸭。

normal.en: a sitting duck is a target too slow to move.
normal.cn: a sitting duck 是懒得动弹、任人瞄准的目标。

normal.en: dodge and duck both mean getting out of the way fast.
normal.cn: dodge 与 duck 都表示快速躲开。

abstract.en: See the bird tip forward and vanish under the water line.
abstract.cn: 看见鸭子向前一倾，消失在水线之下。

abstract.en: Feel your neck bend quickly as a ball flies past.
abstract.cn: 感受皮球飞过时脖子猛地一缩。

abstract.en: Hear the quiet splash of six ducklings paddling away.
abstract.cn: 听六只小鸭划水离去的轻响。

examples.en: The ducks gathered where the children threw bread.
examples.cn: 孩子们扔面包的地方聚集着鸭子。

examples.en: Duck your head or you will hit the door frame.
examples.cn: 低头，不然你会撞到门框。

examples.en: We shared roast duck and pancakes at the small shop.
examples.cn: 我们在小店里分食烤鸭和薄饼。

sensesIntro.en: Duck starts as the plunging water bird, then covers its meat and the human motion of plunging down.
sensesIntro.cn: duck 从会扎水的水鸟出发，涵盖其肉，再引申为人猛然低头的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat-billed bird vanishing under water
core.cn: 核心意象：扁嘴的鸟一头没入水下

branches.en: The bird that swims and dives

branches.cn: 端上盘中的鸭肉

branches.en: The head bent down to escape

branches.en: The body under the surface

branches.en: One quick motion shared by bird and person
branches.cn: 鸟与人共用的一个快速动作

intro.en: Duck keeps a small family with the young-one ending -ling.
intro.cn: duck 有一支小词族，带表示幼小的后缀 -ling。

latinIntro.en: Duck is Germanic in origin, so it has no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: duck 源自日耳曼语，因此没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 家伙；哥们；老兄；花花公子；西部度假游客
definition_en: an informal word for a man, especially a friend, or a fashionable city man visiting the countryside
core_image: 拍肩打招呼：一句随口喊出的哥们称呼
scene: 海滩边两个年轻人冲浪归来，互相击掌，其中一人笑着朝另一人喊了一声。Hey dude, that wave was huge!
sceneCN: 这里 dude 是「哥们、老兄」（第 2 个义项：对男性朋友的随口称呼）；句意是“嘿哥们，刚才那个浪真大！”，体现这个词的口语寒暄用法。

pos.zh: 家伙；哥们；老兄；花花公子；城里来的度假游客
打扮；盛装打扮（常用于短语 dude up）

某个家伙；某个不知名的人

由 dude 加女性后缀 -ette 构成的戏谑说法，指女版哥们
由 dude 加 -ism 后缀构成的戏谑词，指一种源自电影的悠闲生活哲学

senses.title: A man; a guy
senses.definition: an informal word for any man or young male person
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对任意男性或年轻男子的称呼
senses.example: Some dude asked me for directions at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 车站有个家伙向我问路。
senses.why: The word was first used for a particular kind of man, then widened to mean almost any man in casual talk.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初只指某一类讲究的男性，后来在口语中泛化，几乎可以指任何一个男人，词义由窄变宽。

senses.title: A friendly way to address someone
senses.definition: a friendly informal way to address a friend, especially among young people
senses.definitionCN: 对朋友friendly的随口称呼，年轻人之间尤其常用
senses.example: Dude, you will not believe what happened today.
senses.exampleCN: 老兄，你绝对想不到今天发生了什么。
senses.why: Calling someone by a relaxed noun turns the word into pure address, showing closeness rather than description.
senses.whyCN: 当称呼不再描述对方而是纯粹拉近距离时，名词就变成了寒暄语，体现亲近感而非字面身份。

senses.title: A fashionable city man
senses.titleCN: 城里时髦男子；花花公子
senses.definition: a man from the city who dresses very carefully and pays too much attention to style
senses.definitionCN: 衣着讲究、过分注重外表的城里男子
senses.example: The original dude wore fancy clothes and knew nothing about farm work.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的花花公子穿着华丽，却对农活一窍不通。
senses.why: The earliest recorded sense, from late nineteenth century American English, focused on showy clothing and city manners.
senses.whyCN: 这是十九世纪末美式英语里最早记录的义项，核心在于显眼的穿着与都市做派，是后来一切引申的源头。

senses.title: A city visitor at a ranch
senses.definition: a city person vacationing on a western ranch, inexperienced in ranch life
senses.definitionCN: 到西部牧场度假、缺乏牧场生活经验的城市人
senses.example: The ranch hands laughed at the dude trying to saddle a horse.
senses.exampleCN: 牧场工人笑话那个连马鞍都不会装的城市游客。
senses.why: Because such visitors were well dressed and unskilled, the fashionable sense was applied to them as a mild joke.
senses.whyCN: 这类游客衣着体面却笨手笨脚，于是时髦男子的称呼被挪用到他们身上，带着温和的调侃。

senses.title: A showily dressed, unskilled outsider
senses.definition: a person whose fine appearance contrasts with their lack of practical experience
senses.definitionCN: 外表光鲜但缺乏实际本领的人
senses.example: To the cowboys, every dude looked the same: neat suit, useless hands.
senses.exampleCN: 在牛仔眼里，所有讲究人看起来都一样：西装笔挺，两手笨拙。
senses.why: The contrast between polished surface and clumsy action became the very definition of the type.
senses.whyCN: 光鲜外表与笨拙行动之间的反差，本身就成了这一类人的定义，词义聚焦在「虚有其表」。

senses.title: An unnamed person
senses.definition: used for a person whose name is unknown or not worth mentioning
senses.definitionCN: 指姓名不详或不必点名的某个人
senses.example: A dude in a red jacket left this package here.
senses.exampleCN: 一个穿红夹克的家伙把包裹落在这儿了。
senses.why: Casual nouns often become placeholders when a speaker does not know or care about identity.
senses.whyCN: 当说话人不了解或不在意对方身份时，随意名词自然变成指代工具，词义从身份滑向「某人」。

senses.title: An ordinary, relaxed man
senses.definition: a man seen as easygoing and unpretentious, often in phrases like just a regular dude
senses.definitionCN: 随和不做作的男人，常见于 just a regular dude 之类的说法
senses.example: He is a famous actor, but he is really just a regular dude.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个名演员，但其实就是个随和的普通人。
senses.why: As the teasing edge faded, the word kept its relaxed flavor and began to mean down-to-earth rather than showy.
senses.whyCN: 调侃意味淡去后，词保留了轻松随意的语感，语义从「炫耀外表」翻转为「接地气」，是词义的反向漂移。

senses.title: To dress up smartly
senses.definition: to dress oneself in fancy clothes, usually in the phrase dude up
senses.definitionCN: 穿上讲究的衣服，通常用于短语 dude up
senses.example: They all duded up for the awards dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为颁奖晚宴都盛装打扮了一番。
senses.why: The noun for a finely dressed man was turned into a verb describing the act of becoming finely dressed.
senses.whyCN: 指人的名词被活用作动词，描述「变成那种人」的动作，即通过装扮成为讲究穿着的男子。

intro.en: Dude is a young American slang word whose ultimate origin is uncertain; it grew from the idea of a fastidiously dressed man and gradually became a general friendly address.
intro.cn: dude 是年轻的美国俚语词，其最终来源不确定；它从「讲究穿着的男子」这一核心义出发，逐渐演变成通用的友好称呼。

items.en: The word is first recorded in American English around 1883, meaning a man who dresses fastidiously; its ultimate origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 该词约在 1883 年首次见于美国英语，指衣着过分讲究的男子；其最终来源不确定。

items.en: One common hypothesis links it to duds, an older slang word for clothes, but this connection is generally believed rather than proved.
items.cn: 一种常见假说把它与 duds（旧时指衣服的俚语）联系起来，但这只是一般认为，并未确证。

items.en: Some scholars suggest influence from dandy, the word for a fashionable man, or from the nonsense name Yankee Doodle; these are competing hypotheses and should not be forced into one choice.
items.cn: 也有学者提出它可能受了 dandy（时髦男子）或滑稽歌名 Yankee Doodle 的影响；这些是并列假说，不宜强行择定。

items.en: In the early twentieth century the word spread to dude ranch, a resort ranch for city visitors, fixing the sense of the inexperienced city tourist.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，该词扩展出 dude ranch 一语，指接待城市游客的度假牧场，坐实了「城市游客」这一义项。

items.en: From surf and youth culture in California, dude became a relaxed address for friends of any background, shedding its mocking tone.
items.cn: 经加州冲浪与青年文化推广，dude 变成了不分背景的朋友间随意称呼，褪去了嘲讽色彩。

items.en: Today dude is one of the most common informal address words in American English, and the verb phrase dude up keeps the old sense of dressing smartly.
items.cn: 如今 dude 是美式英语最常见的随意称呼之一，动词短语 dude up 则保留着旧的「盛装打扮」之义。

note.en: Dude is surrounded by short slang words for men and clothes; several look alike, others share the same social flavor.
note.cn: dude 周围聚集了一批指男性与衣着的短小俚语词：有的拼写相近，有的社会语感相似。

entries.definition: something that fails to work or impress
entries.definitionCN: 失败品；无用的东西——只比 dude 少一个字母，词源关系一般认为与衣着义相关但存疑，二者用法完全不同

entries.definition: informal word for clothes
entries.definitionCN: 衣服（俚语）——被认为是 dude 的可能来源之一，但联系未确证

entries.definition: a man who cares greatly about elegant dress
entries.definitionCN: 讲究穿戴的花花公子——语义与 dude 的旧义几乎重叠，有学者认为它影响了 dude 的形成

entries.definition: the most general informal word for a man
entries.definitionCN: 家伙、男人——最通用的口语说法，比 dude 更中性，不带拉近距离的寒暄色彩

entries.definition: a friend, used warmly in address
entries.definitionCN: 伙计、好友——与 dude 的称呼用法接近，但更强调友谊本身

entries.definition: a friend or companion, common British address
entries.definitionCN: 伙伴、老兄——英式口语中与 dude 功能对应的称呼词

normalIntro.en: Use the word family and real phrases to lock dude in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 用词族与真实短语把 dude 牢牢锁进记忆。

normal.en: duds means clothes; dude may have grown from dressing in fine duds.
normal.cn: duds 意为衣服；dude 一般认为可能与「穿讲究的衣服」相关。

normal.en: dude ranch is a resort where city dudes learn cowboy life.
normal.cn: dude ranch 是城市「讲究人」体验牛仔生活的度假牧场。

normal.cn: dude up = 盛装打扮；名词活用作动词表示精心装扮。

normal.en: dandy is the elegant cousin; both began as words for fashionable men.
normal.cn: dandy 是它优雅的表亲：两词都从「时髦男子」起家。

normal.en: Hey dude! Repeat the greeting until it feels natural.
normal.cn: 反复念 Hey dude!，直到招呼语变得脱口而出。

abstract.en: Picture a city man in a shiny suit standing awkwardly in a cowboy field.
abstract.cn: 想象一个穿亮西装的城里人尴尬地站在牛仔牧场上。

abstract.en: Hear two surfers slap palms and shout dude after a big wave.
abstract.cn: 耳边回响两个冲浪者击掌大喊 dude 的声音。

abstract.en: Feel the tap on the shoulder: a casual word that turns strangers into pals.
abstract.cn: 感受拍肩的力道：一个把陌生人变成哥们儿的随意称呼。

examples.en: Dude, you left your phone on the table.
examples.cn: 老兄，你把手机落在桌上了。

examples.en: In the 1880s a dude meant a man who dressed far too elegantly.
examples.cn: 在十九世纪八十年代，dude 指穿得过分讲究的男子。

examples.en: The dude ranch was full of city visitors wearing brand-new boots.
examples.cn: 牛仔度假牧场里挤满了穿着崭新靴子的城市游客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斗的」——见面喊一声 dude（斗的），像凑过来拍肩逗弄一下哥们，不是真在打斗。

root: 词源存疑：dude 为十九世纪末美国俚语，一般认为可能与 duds（衣服）相关，另有受 dandy 或 Yankee Doodle 影响的假说，均未确证；无可追溯的拉丁或希腊词根。

sensesIntro.en: From the oldest sense of a fastidiously dressed city man, dude widened to ranch visitors, then to any man, and finally into a friendly address and a verb for dressing up.
sensesIntro.cn: dude 从「讲究穿着的城里男子」这一最早义项出发，先扩展到牧场游客，再泛化为任意男人，最终变成友好称呼与「盛装打扮」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a polished city man stepping into a rough, casual world
core.cn: 核心意象：一个衣着光鲜的城里人，走进粗犷随意的世界

branches.en: The oldest pole: showy clothes and city manners.
branches.cn: 最古老的一极：显眼的穿着与都市做派。

branches.en: The word travels west with city tourists on vacation ranches.
branches.cn: 词随城市游客一路向西，落在度假牧场上。

branches.en: Generalizing from type to any unnamed man.
branches.cn: 从特定类型泛化为任意不点名的男人。

branches.en: The teasing fades into warmth and easy friendship.
branches.cn: 调侃褪去，化为亲切随和的友谊称呼。

branches.en: The noun turns into a verb: becoming the well-dressed man.
branches.cn: 名词转作动词：通过装扮变成那个讲究穿着的人。

intro.en: Dude has no classical prefix or suffix; its relatives are slang words and compounds formed directly from it.
intro.cn: dude 没有古典前缀或后缀；它的相关词是俚语词与由它直接构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Because the origin of dude is uncertain American slang, there is no Latin family to list.
latinIntro.cn: 由于 dude 是来源不确定的美国俚语，没有可列出的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The new gadget turned out to be a dud.
items.exampleCN: 那个新装置结果是个废物。

items.example: Put on your best duds for the party.
items.exampleCN: 为派对穿上你最好的衣服。

items.meaning: a man overly concerned with elegant dress
items.meaningCN: 过分讲究穿着的花花公子

items.exampleCN: 他像花花公子一样昂首阔步。

items.meaning: a ranch resort for city tourists
items.example: They spent a week at a dude ranch in Wyoming.
items.exampleCN: 他们在怀俄明的一座度假牧场待了一周。

items.example: Dude up and join us tonight.
items.exampleCN: 今晚盛装打扮来赴约吧。

items.example: A sunburned surfer dude waved at us.
items.exampleCN: 一个晒黑的冲浪哥们朝我们挥手。

items.meaning: a mock philosophy of relaxed living
items.exampleCN: 这种悠闲哲学主张凡事放轻松。

items.example: Dudette is built with the -ette suffix.
items.exampleCN: dudette 即由 -ette 后缀构成。

definition_zh: 预定的；到期的；应付的；由于；应有的；应得之物
definition_en: expected or scheduled to happen, owed or payable, caused by, rightly required, or the share that is owed to someone
core_image: 日历上一格被圈住的日子，旁边压着一张未付的账单
scene: 站台上的电子屏一遍遍刷新到达时间，人群开始向前挪。The next train is due in ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 due 是「预定到达的」（第 1 个义项：按时刻表预期发生或到达）；句意是下一班火车预定十分钟后到达。

pos.zh: 形容词：预定的；到期的；应付的；由于；应有的
名词：应得之物；应得的份额

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「按时地；适当地」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「过分的；不应有的」
由前缀 over- 加本词构成，义为「过期的；迟到的」
与 due 同出拉丁语 debere，义为「义务；职责；税」

senses.title: Expected or scheduled
senses.definition: expected or arranged to happen or arrive at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 预期或安排在某时发生、到达
senses.example: The train is due at six.
senses.exampleCN: 火车预定六点到。
senses.why: Something due is placed on a timetable; the word marks a point that has been fixed in advance and is now being approached.
senses.whyCN: 事情被放进时刻表，due 标出一个预先定好、正在逐渐临近的时点。

senses.title: Owed or payable
senses.definition: owed as money or as a right, and therefore required to be paid or given
senses.definitionCN: 作为钱款或权利而欠下的，因此必须支付或给予
senses.example: The rent is due on the first of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 房租在每月一号到期。
senses.why: The oldest sense is debt: what one owes has a date attached, so due moves from 'owed' to 'payable now'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是债务：欠下的东西带着一个日期，所以 due 从「欠着」走到「现在该付」。

senses.title: Caused by
senses.definition: used in the phrase due to to mean caused by or because of
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 due to，意为「由……造成」或「因为」
senses.example: The delay was due to heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 延误是由于大雪造成的。
senses.why: If a result is owed to a cause, the debt image explains the cause: the effect is what the cause has produced and must be credited with.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果欠着某个原因，债务意象就解释了原因：结果是原因所产生、并应记在原因账上的东西。

senses.title: Rightly required
senses.definition: proper, adequate or rightly required, as in due care or due process
senses.definitionCN: 恰当的、足够的或理应要求的，如应有的谨慎或正当程序
senses.example: The doctor acted with due care.
senses.exampleCN: 医生以应有的谨慎行事。
senses.why: What is owed can also be what is owed by duty rather than money: the care a situation rightly demands.
senses.whyCN: 所欠之物也可以是责任而非金钱所欠的：某种情形理应要求的谨慎。

senses.title: A deserved share
senses.definition: the share or recognition that is rightly owed to a person, especially in the phrase give someone their due
senses.definitionCN: 理应给予某人的份额或认可，尤用于短语 give someone their due
senses.example: Give him his due: he warned us early.
senses.exampleCN: 说句公道话：他早就警告过我们。
senses.why: The noun keeps the debt image in human form: recognition is something owed to a person and can be handed over.
senses.whyCN: 名词把债务意象保留在人的层面：认可是一种欠着某人的东西，可以被交还给他。

intro.en: Due comes from Latin debere, to owe, through Old French; the modern senses all grow out of the idea of a debt with a date.
intro.cn: due 经由古法语来自拉丁语 debere（欠），现代各个义项都从「带日期的债务」这一观念生长出来。

items.en: Latin debere meant to owe or to be under an obligation, and it is the root of debit, debt and duty as well.
items.cn: 拉丁语 debere 意为「欠」或「负有义务」，也是 debit、debt、duty 的词根。

items.en: The past participle debitum meant something owed, and it became the Latin noun for a debt.
items.cn: 过去分词 debitum 意为「所欠之物」，后来成为拉丁语中表示债务的名词。

items.en: Old French deu, the past participle of devoir, carried the sense of owed and of fitting or proper.
items.cn: 古法语 deu 是 devoir 的过去分词，兼具「所欠的」与「合适的、应有的」两层意思。

items.en: Middle English dewe already meant owed, payable and proper, so the money and duty senses arrived together.
items.cn: 中古英语 dewe 已同时表示「所欠的、应付的、恰当的」，金钱义与责任义是一起进来的。

items.en: The caused-by sense of due to is often dated to the nineteenth century; its earlier history is debated.
items.cn: due to 表「由于」的用法常被定在十九世纪，其更早的历史仍有争议。

items.en: Due date, due process and give someone their due keep the debt image in law, business and everyday fairness.
items.cn: due date、due process 与 give someone their due 让债务意象继续活在法律、商业与日常的公道里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin debt family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of obligation, expectation and payment.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「债务」词族的词；近义组收表示义务、预期与付款的形容词。

entries.definition: In the proper or expected way, or at the proper time; due plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「按时地、适当地」，由 due 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: More than is proper or necessary; un- plus due.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过分的、不应有的」，由 un- 加 due 构成。

entries.definition: Not paid or done by the expected time; over- plus due.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过期的、迟到的」，由 over- 加 due 构成。

entries.definition: An entry recording money owed or paid out; from Latin debitum.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「借方；借记」，来自拉丁语 debitum。

entries.definition: Required to be paid, especially by a stated date; the commercial twin of due.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「应付的」，尤指在指定日期前支付，是 due 的商业近亲。

entries.definition: Not yet paid back; it states the debt without the timetable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被欠的、未偿的」，只说明债务，不强调时间表。

entries.definition: Thought likely to happen; close to due but without the fixed schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「预期的」，接近 due，但不含固定的时刻表。

entries.definition: Still to be paid, as in owing to; also used in the phrase owing to for because of.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「尚欠的」，用于 owing to 时也可表示「由于」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the Latin debt and follow it into timetables, causes and fairness.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从拉丁语的「欠」出发，再跟着它走进时刻表、原因与公道。

normal.en: Latin debere is to owe; due is what is owed, whether money, time or credit.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 debere 是「欠」；due 就是所欠之物，无论是钱、时间还是认可。

normal.en: A due date is the day a debt comes calling.
normal.cn: due date 就是债务上门的那一天。

normal.en: The train is due at six: the timetable owes us an arrival.
normal.cn: 火车预定六点到：时刻表欠我们一个到达。

normal.en: Due to means caused by, because the effect is owed to the cause.
normal.cn: due to 意为「由于」，因为结果欠着原因。

normal.en: Give someone their due means hand over the recognition they are owed.
normal.cn: give someone their due 意为把欠他们的那份认可交还给他们。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar square circled in red, with a bill pinned beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上一格被红笔圈住，旁边钉着一张账单。

abstract.en: The same circle moves onto a platform clock, then onto a courtroom schedule.
abstract.cn: 同一个圈又移到站台的钟上，再移到法庭的日程上。

abstract.en: Due is time turned into an obligation: something will arrive, or something must be paid.
abstract.cn: due 是被时间变成义务的东西：某物即将到达，或某物必须支付。

examples.en: The train is due at six.
examples.cn: 火车预定六点到。

examples.en: The report is due next Friday.
examples.cn: 报告下周五到期。

examples.en: The delay was due to heavy snow.
examples.cn: 延误是由于大雪造成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: due 与 debt、debit 同出拉丁语「欠」：欠钱是到期应付，欠时间是预定到达，欠原因就是「由于」。

root: 经由古法语 deu 来自拉丁语 debere「欠、负有义务」，其过去分词 debitum 意为「所欠之物」，也是 debt、debit、duty 的来源。中古英语 dewe 已兼有「所欠的」与「应有的」两义；表「由于」的 due to 常被定在十九世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of due all turn one debt into a deadline: a scheduled arrival, money to pay, a cause to credit, care that is required, and recognition that is owed.
sensesIntro.cn: due 的五个义项都把同一笔「债」变成期限：预定的到达、该付的钱、该记在账上的原因、理应的谨慎，以及应得的认可。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circled date on a calendar with an unpaid bill pinned beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上圈出的一个日子，旁边钉着一张未付的账单。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: money owed and now payable on a stated date.
branches.cn: 账簿线：欠下的钱，如今在约定日期应付。

branches.en: THE TIMETABLE: an arrival or event owed to us by the schedule.
branches.cn: 时刻表线：时刻表欠我们的一个到达或事件。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: an effect is owed to the reason that produced it.
branches.cn: 原因线：结果欠着产生它的那个原因。

branches.en: THE DUTY: what a situation rightly demands, such as due care or due process.
branches.cn: 责任线：某种情形理应要求的东西，如应有的谨慎或正当程序。

branches.en: THE CREDIT: the recognition a person is owed and should receive.
branches.cn: 认可线：一个人应得并应当得到的认可。

intro.en: Due is a Latin-derived adjective; English adds -ly, un- and over-, and borrows the same root in debit and duty.
intro.cn: due 是源自拉丁语的形容词；英语加 -ly、un-、over-，并在 debit 与 duty 中借用了同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin debere and its participle debitum are recorded forms, so only the deeper Indo-European origin is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 debere 及其分词 debitum 都是有记录的形式，只有更早的印欧语来源属于重构。

items.example: The adjective carries both the debt and the duty senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时带有债务与责任两层意思。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: Duty comes from the same French branch.
items.exampleCN: duty 来自同一支法语来源。

items.meaning: an entry of money owed or paid
items.meaningCN: 记录欠款或支出的账项

latinEntries.meaning: to owe, to be under an obligation

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun from the participle of debere

definition_zh: 乏味的；迟钝的；暗淡的；沉闷的；（疼痛）隐约的；（刀）钝的
definition_en: not interesting, slow to understand, not bright or sharp, not clear as a pain is not sharp, or to make something less sharp or lively
core_image: 一把卷了刃的旧刀，切不开纸，也照不出光
scene: 讲座在昏暗的灯下进行，前排已有人开始打瞌睡。The lecture was accurate but dull.
sceneCN: 这里 dull 是「乏味的」（第 1 个义项：没有趣味、让人提不起精神）；句意是那场讲座虽然准确，却很乏味。

pos.zh: 形容词：乏味的；迟钝的；暗淡的；钝的
动词：使迟钝；使减弱；使变暗

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「乏味；迟钝；暗淡」
由本词加表人后缀 -ard 构成，义为「迟钝的人；笨人」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「乏味地；迟钝地；暗淡地」

senses.title: Not interesting
senses.definition: lacking interest, excitement or variety, so that it is hard to pay attention
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味、刺激或变化，使人难以集中注意
senses.example: The lecture was accurate but dull.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座虽然准确，却很乏味。
senses.why: A dull blade cannot cut, and a dull event cannot hold attention; the same word marks an edge that has lost its bite.
senses.whyCN: 钝刀切不动东西，乏味的事抓不住注意力；同一个词都在标记一把失去锋刃的「刃」。

senses.title: Not sharp, as a blade
senses.definition: having an edge that is not sharp and therefore cuts poorly
senses.definitionCN: 刃口不锋利，因此切割效果差
senses.example: The knife was too dull to cut the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 那把刀太钝，切不开面包。
senses.why: This is the physical source: a dull edge reflects no light along its line and does not part what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理源头：钝刃沿刃线反不出光，也分不开它所接触的东西。

senses.title: Slow to understand
senses.definition: slow to learn, notice or understand things
senses.definitionCN: 学习、察觉或理解事物较慢
senses.example: The drugs had left his mind dull for a few hours.
senses.exampleCN: 那些药让他的头脑迟钝了几个小时。
senses.why: A mind without a sharp edge is pictured like a blade without one: it still works, but it no longer cuts quickly.
senses.whyCN: 没有锋刃的头脑被比作没有刃口的刀：还能用，却不再切得快。

senses.title: Not bright or clear
senses.definition: not bright, not shiny and not clear, as light, colour or weather
senses.definitionCN: 不明亮、不反光、不清晰，如光线、颜色或天气
senses.example: The sky turned a dull grey before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前，天空变成暗淡的灰色。
senses.why: Light on a dull surface scatters instead of shining back, so the word moves easily from metal to sky and paint.
senses.whyCN: 光落在暗淡的表面上会散开而不是反射回来，所以这个词很容易从金属移到天空和油漆。

senses.title: Faint, as pain
senses.definition: felt as a steady but not sharp pain, more aching than stabbing
senses.definitionCN: 持续的、不尖锐的疼痛，更像酸痛而非刺痛
senses.example: She felt a dull ache in her shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 她感到肩膀有一阵隐隐的酸痛。
senses.why: Pain with no sharp point is like a blade with no edge: present and heavy, but not cutting.
senses.whyCN: 没有尖锐痛点的疼，就像没有刃口的刀：存在且沉重，却不切割。

senses.title: To make less sharp
senses.definition: to make something less sharp, bright, strong or interesting
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得不那么锋利、明亮、强烈或有趣
senses.example: The medicine dulled the pain within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。
senses.why: The verb applies the adjective to an object: it removes the edge, the shine or the intensity.
senses.whyCN: 动词把形容词施加到某物上：去掉它的锋刃、光泽或强度。

intro.en: Dull is a native English adjective whose earliest recorded senses are slow and stupid; the physical sense of a blunt edge came alongside.
intro.cn: dull 是本族语英语形容词，最早记录的义项是「迟钝、愚笨」，钝刃这一物理义同时并存。

items.en: A root connected with slowness or foolishness is sometimes suggested, but its exact form and deeper origin are uncertain.
items.cn: 有人提出它与表示「迟缓、愚笨」的词根有关，但其确切形式和更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English dol meant foolish or slow-witted and is a likely relative rather than a direct ancestor.
items.cn: 古英语 dol 意为「愚笨、迟钝」，很可能是亲属词而非直系祖先。

items.en: Middle English dul spread from people to edges, colours and weather, where sharpness or brightness was missing.
items.cn: 中古英语 dul 从人扩展到刃口、颜色和天气，指缺少锋利或明亮。

items.en: The senses of a blunt blade and a dim surface are recorded by the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 钝刃与暗淡表面这两个义项在十四世纪已有记录。

items.en: The figurative sense of boring speech grew from the image of an edge that no longer cuts.
items.cn: 言语乏味的比喻义，是从「刃口不再切割」这一意象生长出来的。

items.en: Dull pain, dull weather and dull the pain show the word applied to sensation and to relief.
items.cn: dull pain、dull weather 与 dull the pain 展示了这个词用在感觉与缓解上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dull; the near-meaning group separates boring, blunt and dim, which cover different missing qualities.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dull 构成的词形；近义组区分 boring、blunt 与 dim，它们各自缺少的品质不同。

entries.definition: The state of being dull in any of its senses; dull plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指乏味、迟钝或暗淡的状态，由 dull 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: A slow or stupid person; dull plus the person suffix -ard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指迟钝或愚笨的人，由 dull 加表人后缀 -ard 构成。

entries.definition: In a dull manner, without brightness, sharpness or interest.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「乏味地、迟钝地、暗淡地」。

entries.definition: Having eyes that show no interest or brightness; dull plus eyed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「目光呆滞的」，由 dull 与 eyed 复合。

entries.definition: Making someone feel tired and uninterested; more direct and personal than dull.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人厌烦的」，比 dull 更直接、更针对人的感受。

entries.definition: Having a thick edge that does not cut well; the physical twin of dull.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「钝的」，是 dull 物理义的同义词。

entries.definition: Not bright, as light or colour; it covers the brightness sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「昏暗的」，只覆盖明亮度这一义项。

entries.definition: Moving or responding more slowly than normal; it describes pace, not interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迟缓的」，描述速度而非趣味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the image of a blunt edge and follow it into minds, weather and pain.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子守住「钝刃」这一意象，再跟着它走进头脑、天气与疼痛。

normal.en: A dull knife cannot cut; start there and every other sense makes sense.
normal.cn: 钝刀切不动，从这里出发，其他义项都说得通。

normal.en: A dull mind is a blade without an edge: still there, but slow to cut.
normal.cn: 迟钝的头脑就是没有刃口的刀：还在，却切得慢。

normal.en: A dull sky gives no shine, and a dull grey wall gives none either.
normal.cn: 阴沉的天空没有光泽，暗淡的灰墙也没有。

normal.en: A dull ache is pain with no point, like a blade with no edge.
normal.cn: 隐隐的酸痛是没有尖端的疼，就像没有刃口的刀。

normal.en: To dull the pain is to take the edge off it, the same image as a verb.
normal.cn: to dull the pain 就是把疼痛的锋刃去掉，还是同一个意象。

abstract.en: Picture a blade lying on a table, its edge rounded by years of use.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀躺在桌上，刃口被多年使用磨圆了。

abstract.en: Draw the same rounded line across a page of prose and a grey afternoon sky.
abstract.cn: 把同一条磨圆的线画在一页文字上，也画在一个灰色的午后天空上。

abstract.en: Dull is always a missing edge: in metal, in light, in wit or in pain.
abstract.cn: dull 永远是一种缺失的锋刃：在金属里、在光里、在机敏里，或在疼痛里。

examples.en: The lecture was accurate but dull.
examples.cn: 那场讲座虽然准确，却很乏味。

examples.en: The knife was too dull to cut the bread.
examples.cn: 那把刀太钝，切不开面包。

examples.en: The medicine dulled the pain within an hour.
examples.cn: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。

dict_mnemonic.text: dull 是一把卷了刃的刀：刀钝了，光暗了，人反应慢了，话也就乏味了。

root: 本族语英语形容词，最早义项为「迟钝、愚笨」，与古英语 dol 可能是亲属关系；中古英语 dul 扩展到钝刃、暗淡的颜色与阴沉的天气。更早的印欧语来源一般与「迟缓」相关，确切形式不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of dull all describe a missing edge: in a blade, in light, in a mind, in interest, in pain, or in the act of removing sharpness.
sensesIntro.cn: dull 的六个义项都在描述一种缺失的锋刃：在刀刃上、在光里、在头脑里、在趣味里、在疼痛里，或在去掉锋刃的动作里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old knife with a rounded edge that neither cuts nor shines.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刃口磨圆的旧刀，既切不动也不反光。

branches.en: THE EDGE: the physical blade that no longer parts what it touches.
branches.cn: 刃口线：物理上的刀刃不再分开它接触的东西。

branches.en: THE LIGHT: a surface that scatters light instead of shining back.
branches.cn: 光线线：表面把光散开，而不是反射回来。

branches.en: THE MIND: a person who still thinks but no longer cuts quickly.
branches.cn: 头脑线：人还能思考，却不再反应迅速。

branches.en: THE PAGE: speech or writing with no edge to hold attention.
branches.cn: 书页线：言谈或文字没有能抓住注意力的锋刃。

branches.en: THE BODY: a pain without a point, and the act of taking that point away.
branches.cn: 身体线：没有尖端的疼痛，以及把尖端去掉的动作。

intro.en: Dull is a native adjective; English adds -ness, -ard, -ly, -ed and -ing to build its family.
intro.cn: dull 是本族语形容词；英语加 -ness、-ard、-ly、-ed、-ing 来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; Latin hebes, blunt or dull, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁语 hebes（钝的、迟钝的）只是语义对照。

items.example: The adjective is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是词族的基础。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「乏味；迟钝；暗淡」
由本词加表人后缀 -ard 构成，义为「迟钝的人；笨人」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「乏味地；迟钝地；暗淡地」

definition_zh: 哑的；说不出话的；沉默的；愚蠢的
definition_en: unable to speak, silent especially from shock, showing no words, or foolish in an informal sense
core_image: 一个人张着嘴，喉咙里却发不出任何声音
scene: 她站在门口，嘴唇动了动，却一个字也吐不出来。He was struck dumb by the news.
sceneCN: 这里 dumb 是「一时说不出话的」（第 2 个义项：因震惊而语塞）；句意是那个消息让他一时说不出话来。

pos.zh: 形容词：哑的；说不出话的；沉默的；愚蠢的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「默默地；无言地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「哑；沉默」
由本词与 bell 复合，义为「哑铃」

senses.title: Unable to speak
senses.definition: physically unable to speak, either from birth or because of illness or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因先天原因或疾病、受伤而在生理上无法说话
senses.example: The illness left him dumb for almost a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那场病让他将近一年说不出话。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the body cannot produce speech, and the word names the absence of voice itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：身体无法发出言语，这个词直接命名了声音的缺席。

senses.title: Silent from shock
senses.definition: temporarily unable to speak because of strong emotion, especially shock or fear
senses.definitionCN: 因强烈情绪尤其是震惊或恐惧而一时说不出话
senses.example: He was struck dumb by the news.
senses.exampleCN: 那个消息让他一时说不出话来。
senses.why: The body is fine, but emotion takes the voice away for a moment; the same adjective covers a temporary silence.
senses.whyCN: 身体没毛病，是情绪一时夺走了声音；同一个形容词覆盖了这种暂时的沉默。

senses.title: Foolish, in informal use
senses.definition: foolish or stupid, used informally and often lightheartedly
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢的、犯傻的，属口语用法，常带轻松口气
senses.example: It was a dumb question, but nobody laughed.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个傻问题，但没人笑。
senses.why: Speechlessness and slowness of mind were once linked, so the old word for mute slid into informal use for foolish.
senses.whyCN: 说不出话与头脑迟缓曾被联系在一起，于是这个表示「哑」的旧词滑入了口语的「愚蠢」。

senses.title: Without words
senses.definition: performed or expressed without speech, as in a dumb show or dumb waiter
senses.definitionCN: 不用言语来表演或表达的，如哑剧或无声传菜架
senses.example: The actors told the whole story in a dumb show.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们用一出哑剧讲完了整个故事。
senses.why: Anything that works without speech can be called dumb, from a silent performance to a mechanical lift.
senses.whyCN: 任何不靠言语运作的东西都可以叫 dumb，从无声的表演到机械升降架。

intro.en: Dumb is an Old English adjective shared across the Germanic languages, and its sense widened from mute to silent and then to foolish.
intro.cn: dumb 是古英语形容词，为多种日耳曼语言共有，其词义从「哑」扩展到「沉默」，再扩展到「愚蠢」。

items.en: A root connected with being mute or confused is sometimes reconstructed, but its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 有时会重构出一个与「哑、茫然」相关的词根，但其确切形式不确定。

items.en: The Germanic adjective is reconstructed as dumbaz, meaning unable to speak.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的这个形容词被重构为 dumbaz，意为「不能说话的」。

items.en: Old English dumb meant mute, and it could already describe animals without human speech.
items.cn: 古英语 dumb 意为「哑的」，当时已可形容不会说人话的动物。

items.en: The sense widened from permanent muteness to any silence, including silence caused by emotion.
items.cn: 词义从永久性失语扩展到任何沉默，包括情绪造成的沉默。

items.en: The informal sense of foolish is recorded later; it grew from the older link between speechlessness and slowness.
items.cn: 口语中「愚蠢」的义项记录较晚，是从「说不出话」与「迟钝」的旧有关联发展来的。

items.en: Dumb luck, dumb show and dumbbell keep the old word alive in fixed expressions and compounds.
items.cn: dumb luck、dumb show 与 dumbbell 让这个旧词在固定表达和复合词里继续活着。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dumb; the near-meaning group separates mute, silent and speechless by cause and duration.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dumb 构成的词形；近义组按原因与持续时间区分 mute、silent 与 speechless。

entries.definition: In a silent or speechless way; dumb plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「默默地、无言地」，由 dumb 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to speak or of being silent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指不能说话或沉默的状态。

entries.definition: A short bar with weights at each end; dumb plus bell, with a different sense of dumb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「哑铃」，由 dumb 与 bell 复合，此处 dumb 取另一层含义。

entries.definition: Completely astonished and unable to speak; dumb plus the old verb found.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「目瞪口呆的」，由 dumb 与旧动词 found 复合。

entries.definition: Unable to speak, often by birth or injury; more clinical and neutral than dumb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「哑的」，常指先天或受伤所致，比 dumb 更临床、更中性。

entries.definition: Making no sound; it describes the absence of noise rather than the ability to speak.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「沉默的、无声的」，描述没有声音，而非说话能力。

entries.definition: Unable to speak for a moment, usually from strong emotion; close to the shock sense of dumb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「说不出话的」，通常因强烈情绪而起，接近 dumb 的震惊义。

entries.definition: Without a voice, literally or figuratively; often used for groups without power to speak.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无声的、失声的」，也常指没有发言权的群体。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the physical loss of voice and then follow the word into shock, jokes and silent performance.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从生理上失去声音出发，再跟着这个词走进震惊、玩笑和无声表演。

normal.en: Dumb first means the voice cannot come out at all.
normal.cn: dumb 最初指声音根本发不出来。

normal.en: Shock can make a speaking person dumb for a moment.
normal.cn: 震惊能让一个会说话的人一时变哑。

normal.en: Struck dumb is the fixed phrase for being silenced by surprise.
normal.cn: struck dumb 是被惊讶得说不出话的固定说法。

normal.en: Dumb luck is luck with no cleverness behind it.
normal.cn: dumb luck 是背后没有半点聪明的运气。

normal.en: A dumb show tells a story with no words at all.
normal.cn: dumb show 完全不用语言来讲故事。

abstract.en: Picture an open mouth with a small locked door where the voice should come out.
abstract.cn: 想象一张张开的嘴，声音本该出来的地方却是一扇锁住的小门。

abstract.en: The same locked door appears for a moment on a shocked face, then opens again.
abstract.cn: 同一扇锁住的门在一张震惊的脸上短暂出现，然后又打开。

abstract.en: Dumb is about a missing voice, and every sense removes it in a different way.
abstract.cn: dumb 讲的是缺失的声音，每个义项都以不同方式拿走了它。

examples.en: He was struck dumb by the news.
examples.cn: 那个消息让他一时说不出话来。

examples.en: It was a dumb question, but nobody laughed.
examples.cn: 那是个傻问题，但没人笑。

examples.en: She stared at him, dumb with anger.
examples.cn: 她盯着他，气得说不出话。

dict_mnemonic.text: dumb 是一张嘴却发不出声：生理上是哑，情绪上是惊得说不出话，口语里就成了「犯傻」。

root: 古英语 dumb「哑的」，为日耳曼语共有词，重构形式作 dumbaz；中古英语起从永久失语扩展到任何沉默，十九世纪又发展出口语「愚蠢」义。更早的印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of dumb all describe a missing voice: a body that cannot speak, a person silenced by shock, a mind that seems to have no words, and a performance done without speech.
sensesIntro.cn: dumb 的四个义项都在描述缺席的声音：不能说话的身体、被震惊夺去声音的人、似乎没有言语的头脑，以及不用语言的表演。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open mouth with no sound coming out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张张开的嘴，却发不出任何声音。

branches.en: THE BODY: the voice is physically absent, whether from birth or from illness.
branches.cn: 身体线：声音在生理上缺席，无论先天还是疾病所致。

branches.en: THE EMOTION: shock or fear takes the voice away for a moment.
branches.cn: 情绪线：震惊或恐惧一时夺走了声音。

branches.en: THE JOKE: the old silence slides into informal talk about foolishness.
branches.cn: 玩笑线：古老的沉默滑入口语里关于「犯傻」的说法。

branches.en: THE STAGE: a story told with gestures and no words at all.
branches.cn: 舞台线：只用手势、完全不用语言讲的故事。

branches.en: ONE ABSENCE: whether permanent, temporary or staged, the voice is what is missing.
branches.cn: 同一种缺席：无论永久、暂时还是表演性的，缺的都是声音。

intro.en: Dumb is a native Germanic adjective; English adds -ly, -ness, -er, -est and compounds such as dumbbell.
intro.cn: dumb 是本族语日耳曼语形容词；英语加 -ly、-ness、-er、-est，并构成 dumbbell 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; Latin mutus, mute, is a semantic counterpart only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 mutus（哑的）只是语义上的对应。

items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是词族的基础。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「默默地；无言地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「哑；沉默」
由本词与 bell 复合，义为「哑铃」

definition_zh: 倾倒；丢弃；倾销；垃圾场；甩掉（某人）；转储（数据）
definition_en: to drop or unload something heavily, to get rid of something unwanted, to sell goods abroad very cheaply, a place where waste is tipped, or to transfer data to storage
core_image: 卡车掀起车斗，一堆碎石轰然落在空地上
scene: 卡车在空地中央掀起车斗，碎石顺着斜坡倾泻而下。They dumped the sand beside the road.
sceneCN: 这里 dump 是「倾倒」（第 1 个义项：把大量东西重重卸下）；句意是他们把沙子倒在了路边。

pos.zh: 动词：倾倒；丢弃；倾销；甩掉；转储
名词：垃圾场；堆放处；转储

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「自卸车；倾倒者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「倾倒；倾销」
由本词加 -ster 构成，义为「大型垃圾箱」

senses.title: To drop or unload heavily
senses.definition: to drop, tip or unload a large amount of something in one place, often quickly and without care
senses.definitionCN: 把大量东西一下子倒、卸在某一处，常迅速而不加整理
senses.example: They dumped the sand beside the road.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把沙子倒在了路边。
senses.why: The word began as the sound and motion of a heavy fall, so the first picture is a load leaving a cart all at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就是重物落下的声音与动作，所以第一个画面是一车货一下子离开车厢。

senses.title: To get rid of something
senses.definition: to get rid of something unwanted, especially in a careless or illegal way
senses.definitionCN: 把不要的东西处理掉，尤指随意或非法地
senses.example: Someone had dumped old tyres in the river.
senses.exampleCN: 有人把旧轮胎扔进了河里。
senses.why: What is tipped out of sight is also out of mind, so unloading becomes a way of discarding.
senses.whyCN: 倒到看不见的地方，也就从心里消失了，于是「卸下」变成了「丢弃」。

senses.title: To sell abroad cheaply
senses.definition: to sell goods in another country at a price far below what they cost or below the local price
senses.definitionCN: 以远低于成本或低于当地价格的价格在别国出售商品
senses.example: The company was accused of dumping steel on the European market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被指控向欧洲市场倾销钢材。
senses.why: Dumping goods is like tipping a load: the surplus is pushed off into another market to protect the home price.
senses.whyCN: 倾销就像倒货：把过剩的东西推进另一个市场，以保住本国的价格。

senses.title: A place for waste
senses.definition: a place where rubbish, waste or unwanted material is tipped and stored
senses.definitionCN: 倾倒并堆放垃圾、废物或废弃材料的地方
senses.example: The old dump has been turned into a small park.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧垃圾场已被改造成一个小公园。
senses.why: The verb's destination becomes a noun: the place where loads are regularly tipped.
senses.whyCN: 动词的去处变成了名词：卡车经常倾倒货物的那个地方。

senses.title: To end a relationship abruptly
senses.definition: to end a romantic relationship with someone suddenly and without much explanation
senses.definitionCN: 突然且不加解释地结束与某人的恋爱关系
senses.example: She dumped him after two months.
senses.exampleCN: 两个月后她把他甩了。
senses.why: A person treated as unwanted baggage is 'dumped' at the roadside, and the informal sense follows that image.
senses.whyCN: 被当作不要的行李丢在路边的人，就是被 dump 了，口语义正是顺着这个意象来的。

senses.title: To transfer data
senses.definition: to copy a large amount of data from a computer's memory to storage or another system
senses.definitionCN: 把大量数据从计算机内存复制到存储设备或另一系统
senses.example: The program dumped the whole database to a backup drive.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把整个数据库转储到了备份盘上。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the image of tipping out a container: memory is emptied into storage all at once.
senses.whyCN: 计算机借用了「倒空容器」的意象：内存被一次性倒进存储设备。

intro.en: Dump is probably an imitative word for a heavy fall; its later senses all branch from the image of a load tipped out.
intro.cn: dump 很可能是一个模仿重物落下的词；后来的义项都从「一车货被倒出」这个意象分出来。

items.en: The word is often felt to echo a dull heavy thud, though this cannot be proved.
items.cn: 人们常觉得这个词回响着沉闷的重击声，但这一点无法证实。

items.en: A verb meaning to fall or throw down heavily is recorded in Middle English, with an uncertain earlier history.
items.cn: 中古英语有表示「重重落下或扔下」的动词记录，其更早的历史不确定。

items.en: To dump came to mean tipping a load out of a cart or barrow in one movement.
items.cn: to dump 逐渐指把一车货一次性地从推车或车厢里倒出。

items.en: Mining and industry fixed the noun dump for a tip or waste heap, and trade gave the word its dumping sense.
items.cn: 采矿与工业把名词 dump 固定为堆放场或废石堆，贸易则赋予它「倾销」义。

items.en: The informal sense of ending a relationship and the computing sense of copying data appear in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 口语中「甩掉恋人」与计算机中「复制数据」的义项，都出现在二十世纪。

items.en: Data dump, rubbish dump and dump someone show one image spread across very different fields.
items.cn: data dump、rubbish dump 与 dump someone 展示了同一个意象跨越了极不同的领域。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dump; the near-meaning group separates discard, tip and throw away by register and image.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dump 构成的词形；近义组按语体与意象区分 discard、tip 与 throw away。

entries.definition: A vehicle that tips its load, or a person who dumps something; dump plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指自卸车或倾倒者，由 dump 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The act of tipping waste, or the trade practice of selling abroad cheaply.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指倾倒废物的行为，或低价向国外销售的做法。

entries.definition: A large metal container for waste; dump plus the noun suffix -ster.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指大型金属垃圾箱，由 dump 加名词后缀 -ster 构成。

entries.definition: A small mass of dough cooked in water; it looks similar but has a separate origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「汤团、饺子」，外形相近但来源不同。

entries.definition: To throw something away as no longer wanted; more formal and deliberate than dump.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「丢弃」，比 dump 更正式、更有意为之。

entries.definition: To empty a container by turning it over; the physical action behind dump.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「倾倒、翻倒」，是 dump 背后的物理动作。

entries.definition: To get rid of something by putting it in the rubbish; general and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「扔掉」，通用而中性。

entries.definition: To remove goods from a vehicle; it stresses the removal, not the waste.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「卸货」，强调搬下货物，而非当作废物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the sound and motion of a tipped load, then follow it into waste, trade, love and computing.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子守住一车货被倒出时的声音与动作，再跟着它走进垃圾、贸易、感情与计算机。

normal.en: Dump sounds like the thud of a load hitting the ground.
normal.cn: dump 的发音就像一车货砸在地上的闷响。

normal.en: The verb is regular: dump, dumped, dumped, dumping.
normal.cn: 这个动词是规则的：dump、dumped、dumped、dumping。

normal.en: A rubbish dump is the place where loads are tipped again and again.
normal.cn: a rubbish dump 就是一车车货被反复倒下的地方。

normal.en: Dumping goods abroad is tipping a surplus into another market.
normal.cn: dumping goods abroad 就是把过剩的货倒进另一个市场。

normal.en: To dump someone is to treat a person like unwanted baggage at the roadside.
normal.cn: to dump someone 就是把一个人当作路边不要的行李。

abstract.en: Picture a lorry with its bed raised, and a grey stream of gravel sliding out.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆抬起车斗的卡车，一条灰色的碎石流从中滑落。

abstract.en: The same tipping motion reappears as a trash heap, a cheap export deal and a memory emptied onto a disk.
abstract.cn: 同一个倾倒动作又以垃圾堆、廉价出口交易和内存倒入磁盘的形式重现。

abstract.en: Dump is always about unloading something fast, and the question is only onto what.
abstract.cn: dump 永远是把东西快速卸下，问题只在于卸到什么上面。

examples.en: They dumped the sand beside the road.
examples.cn: 他们把沙子倒在了路边。

examples.en: The truck dumped its load at the site.
examples.cn: 卡车在工地卸下了货物。

examples.en: The old computer was dumped in the yard.
examples.cn: 那台旧电脑被扔在了院子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: dump 像重物「咚」地落地：把货倒下来、把废物扔掉、把货低价倾销，都是同一个「倒」。

root: 中古英语有「重重落下、扔下」的动词记录，更早来源不确定，词形可能模仿重物落地声。十六至十七世纪指一次倒出一车货，十九世纪固定「垃圾场」与「倾销」义，二十世纪又出现「甩掉恋人」与「数据转储」义。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of dump all keep one motion: a load tipped out of its container, whether the container is a truck, a market, a relationship or a computer's memory.
sensesIntro.cn: dump 的六个义项都保留同一个动作：一车货被倒出容器，无论这个容器是卡车、市场、一段感情还是计算机内存。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a truck bed rising, and a load sliding out onto the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡车车斗抬起，一车货滑落到地上。

branches.en: THE LOAD: a heavy amount is tipped out in one movement.
branches.cn: 货物线：大量东西被一次性倒出。

branches.en: THE WASTE: what is unloaded is also what is unwanted.
branches.cn: 废物线：被卸下的东西同时也是不要的东西。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a surplus is tipped into another country at a low price.
branches.cn: 市场线：过剩货物以低价倒进另一个国家。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND THE PERSON: a tip becomes a dump, and unwanted baggage becomes a dumped partner.
branches.cn: 地点与人线：堆放处变成垃圾场，不要的行李变成被甩掉的恋人。

branches.en: THE DISK: memory is emptied into storage in one go.
branches.cn: 磁盘线：内存被一次性倒进存储设备。

intro.en: Dump is a native verb of uncertain origin; English adds -er, -ing, -ster and compounds with waste and data.
intro.cn: dump 是来源不确定的本族语动词；英语加 -er、-ing、-ster，并与 waste、data 等构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; Latin effundere, to pour out, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁语 effundere（倒出）只是语义上的对应。

items.meaning: to fall or throw down heavily
items.example: The verb is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的基础。

items.meaning: a container or person connected with

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 waste dump 中。
它出现在 rubbish dump 中。
它出现在 data dump 中。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「自卸车；倾倒者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「倾倒；倾销」
由本词加 -ster 构成，义为「大型垃圾箱」

definition_zh: 在……期间；在……过程中
definition_en: throughout a period, at some point within a period, or in the course of an event or activity
core_image: 一条时间线被括号括住，事情就发生在这段括号里
scene: 窗外雷声滚过，屋里的灯忽然灭了，黑暗中有人摸索着找蜡烛。The lights went out during the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 during 是「在……期间」（第 1 个义项：贯穿某段时间）；句意是暴风雨期间灯灭了。

pos.zh: 介词：在……期间；在……过程中

derivatives.zh: 与 during 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「耐用的；持久的」
与 during 同源，义为「持续时间；期间」

senses.title: Throughout a period
senses.definition: for the whole of a period of time, from its beginning to its end
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间的整段之内，从开始到结束
senses.example: The lights went out during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间灯灭了。
senses.why: During began as the present participle of a verb meaning to last, so it literally places an event 'while the period is lasting'.
senses.whyCN: during 最初是表示「持续」的动词的现在分词，字面上就是把事件放在「那段时间正持续着」的时候。

senses.title: At a point within a period
senses.definition: at some unspecified moment inside a period, not necessarily for all of it
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间内某个未指明的时刻，不一定是整段
senses.example: He fell asleep during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间他睡着了。
senses.why: A point event can sit anywhere inside the bracket of the period, and during covers that inside without fixing the exact moment.
senses.whyCN: 一个瞬时事件可以落在这一时期的括号内任意位置，during 覆盖这个「里面」，却不指明确切时刻。

senses.title: In the course of an activity
senses.definition: while an activity, process or event is going on, especially one with a clear course
senses.definitionCN: 在某项活动、过程或事件进行之时，尤指有明确进程的事
senses.example: During the course, students work in small groups.
senses.exampleCN: 课程过程中，学生们分成小组活动。
senses.why: The period can also be an activity with stages, and during then marks the span in which those stages unfold.
senses.whyCN: 这一时期也可以是一项有阶段的活动，during 就标出这些阶段展开的那段时间。

intro.en: During is the present participle of an obsolete English verb dure, to last, which came from Latin durare through French.
intro.cn: during 是英语旧动词 dure（持续）的现在分词，后者经由法语来自拉丁语 durare。

items.en: Latin durare meant to last or to endure and is the root of duration and durable as well.
items.cn: 拉丁语 durare 意为「持续、忍耐」，也是 duration 与 durable 的词根。

items.en: Old French durer meant to last, and English borrowed it as the verb dure.
items.cn: 古法语 durer 意为「持续」，英语把它借来作动词 dure。

items.en: The English verb dure, to last, is now obsolete but was common in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语动词 dure（持续）如今已废弃，但在十四、十五世纪很常见。

items.en: The form during meant 'while lasting', and from that phrase it became a preposition of time.
items.cn: 形式 during 原意是「当其持续时」，由此变成一个表示时间的介词。

items.en: During is recorded as a preposition by the late fourteenth century, usually with a period or an activity.
items.cn: during 在十四世纪晚期已记录为介词，通常后接一段时期或一项活动。

items.en: The old verb disappeared, but the participle survived as one of the most common time words in English.
items.cn: 旧动词消失了，但这个分词存活下来，成为英语中最常用的时间词之一。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same lasting root; the near-meaning group separates throughout, while and amid by scope and register.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「持续」词族的词；近义组按范围与语体区分 throughout、while 与 amid。

entries.definition: The length of time something lasts; the noun behind the preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「持续时间」，是这个介词背后的名词。

entries.definition: Able to last a long time; it describes objects rather than time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「耐用的、持久的」，描述物体而非时间。

entries.definition: To last through hardship or to bear it; a verb from the same Latin family.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受、持续」，属同一拉丁词族。

entries.definition: An obsolete English verb meaning to last; the form from which during was made.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时英语动词，义为「持续」，正是构成 during 的那个形式。

entries.definition: In every part of a period or place; stronger than during because it excludes gaps.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「贯穿整个期间或各处」，比 during 更强，排除间断。

entries.definition: During the time that something else is happening; it usually joins two clauses.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「当……时」，通常连接两个分句。

entries.definition: In the middle of an event or situation; more formal and often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之中」，更正式，常带文学色彩。

entries.definition: Inside a period or limit; it stresses the boundary rather than the whole span.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之内」，强调边界而非整段。

normalIntro.en: These hooks remember that during was once a participle meaning 'while lasting', then show how it brackets a period.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子记住 during 原是意为「当其持续时」的分词，再展示它如何把一段时间括起来。

normal.en: During was born from dure, to last: it marks the time while something lasts.
normal.cn: during 出自 dure（持续），标记某事物持续着的那段时间。

normal.en: Think of a pair of brackets around a timeline: everything inside happens during it.
normal.cn: 想象在一条时间线上画一对括号：括号里发生的事就是 during 它。

normal.en: During the war covers the whole period; during the lecture can be one moment inside it.
normal.cn: during the war 覆盖整段时期，during the lecture 可以是其中某一刻。

normal.en: Do not confuse during with for: during names the period, for names the length.
normal.cn: 不要把 during 与 for 混淆：during 指那段时间，for 指长度。

normal.en: The same family gives duration and durable, so time is the shared idea.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 duration 与 durable，共同观念就是时间。

abstract.en: Picture two hands holding a stretch of a timeline, with an event placed between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手捏住时间线上的一段，把一件事放在两手之间。

abstract.en: The bracket can be wide as a war or narrow as a single breath.
abstract.cn: 这个括号可以宽如一场战争，也可以窄如一息。

abstract.en: During never says how long; it only says inside which period.
abstract.cn: during 从不说多久，只说在哪段时期之内。

examples.en: The lights went out during the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨期间灯灭了。

examples.en: He fell asleep during the lecture.
examples.cn: 讲座期间他睡着了。

examples.en: During the war, the family lived in the countryside.
examples.cn: 战争期间，这家人住在乡下。

dict_mnemonic.text: during 原是「持续」的现在分词：某事持续着的那段时间，就是 during 它。

root: 英语旧动词 dure「持续」的现在分词，dure 经由古法语 durer 来自拉丁语 durare「持续、忍耐」。during 原意「当其持续时」，十四世纪晚期起用作时间介词；同族词有 duration、durable、endure。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of during all place an event inside a period: across the whole of it, at a point within it, or in the course of an activity.
sensesIntro.cn: during 的三个义项都把事件放进一段时间里：贯穿整段、落在其中某一刻，或在一项活动的过程中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretch of timeline held between two brackets.
core.cn: 核心意象：时间线上被一对括号括住的一段。

branches.en: THE WHOLE BRACKET: an event fills the entire period from start to end.
branches.cn: 整段括号线：事件从开始到结束填满整个时期。

branches.en: THE POINT INSIDE: a brief event happens somewhere within the bracket.
branches.cn: 括号内一点线：短暂事件发生在括号内的某处。

branches.en: THE COURSE: the period is an activity with stages unfolding.
branches.cn: 过程线：这段时期是一项分阶段展开的活动。

branches.en: TWO WIDTHS: a war or a course can both be bracketed, at different scales.
branches.cn: 两种宽度：战争与课程都能被括住，只是尺度不同。

branches.en: ONE MOMENT IN A PROCESS: the point event sits inside a longer course.
branches.cn: 过程里的一刻：瞬时事件落在一段更长的过程之中。

intro.en: During is a fossilised participle: the suffix -ing survives on an old verb that English otherwise dropped.
intro.cn: during 是一个凝固的分词：-ing 后缀留在一个英语其他场合已丢弃的旧动词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin durare and duratio are recorded; the English verb dure came through Old French and then disappeared.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 durare 与 duratio 均有记录；英语动词 dure 经由古法语而来，后来消失。

items.example: The root is shared with duration and durable.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 duration、durable 共用。

items.example: It is the ultimate source of during.
items.exampleCN: 它是 during 的最终来源。

items.example: The verb supplied the participle during.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了分词 during。
它由 dure 构成 during。

items.example: It shares the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 它与 during 共享同一拉丁词根。

derivatives.zh: 与 during 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「耐用的；持久的」
与 during 同源，义为「持续时间；期间」

definition_zh: 灰尘；尘土；掸去灰尘；撒（粉末）；（书面）尘土、遗骸
definition_en: fine dry particles of earth or other material, household dirt, the act of removing it, or to scatter a powder over something
core_image: 阳光斜穿过窗缝，空气里浮着无数细小的颗粒
scene: 阳光从窗缝里照进来，空气里浮着细小的颗粒，落在架子上。Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
sceneCN: 这里 dust 是「灰尘」（第 1 个义项：细干的土状颗粒）；句意是灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。

pos.zh: 名词：灰尘；尘土；粉末
动词：掸去灰尘；撒（粉末）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「布满灰尘的；土色的」
由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「抹布；掸子」
由本词与 pan 复合，义为「簸箕」

senses.title: Fine dry particles
senses.definition: fine dry particles of earth, rock or other material that can float in the air or settle on surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 细干土、岩石或其他材料构成的颗粒，能浮在空气中或落在表面
senses.example: Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。
senses.why: This is the physical core: matter reduced to particles small enough to be carried by air and to settle everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理核心：物质被碎成小到能被空气携带、又能落得到处都是的颗粒。

senses.title: A cloud of particles
senses.definition: a mass of dust lifted into the air, as by wind, traffic or an explosion
senses.definitionCN: 被风、车流或爆炸扬到空中的一团尘土
senses.example: A cloud of dust rose from the dry road.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的路面上扬起一团尘土。
senses.why: The same particles, once airborne, become a visible body; the noun then names the cloud rather than the surface layer.
senses.whyCN: 同样的颗粒一旦升空就成了一团可见的物体，名词于是指这团云，而不是表面那层。

senses.title: To remove dust
senses.definition: to wipe or brush dust from a surface, or to clean a room of it
senses.definitionCN: 把灰尘从表面擦掉或掸掉，或清扫房间里的灰
senses.example: She dusted the furniture before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到之前，她掸去了家具上的灰。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: the particles are there, and the action takes them away.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词反过来：颗粒已经在那里，动作则把它们拿走。

senses.title: To scatter a powder
senses.definition: to scatter a fine powder over something, as sugar, flour or a chemical
senses.definitionCN: 把细粉撒在某物上，如糖、面粉或化学品
senses.example: Dust the cake with a little sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 在蛋糕上撒一点糖。
senses.why: If dust can be removed, it can also be applied: the verb works in both directions, taking away or sprinkling on.
senses.whyCN: 既然灰尘能被去掉，也能被施加：这个动词两个方向都成立，拿走或者撒上。

senses.title: The ground or mortal remains
senses.definition: used in literary and religious language for the ground, the human body or what remains of it
senses.definitionCN: 用于文学与宗教语言，指土地、人体或其遗留之物
senses.example: The old prayer repeats that we are dust and return to dust.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的祷文反复说，我们本是尘土，也要归于尘土。
senses.why: Because the body returns to the ground, dust became a solemn image for mortality, fixed in the phrase dust to dust.
senses.whyCN: 因为身体归入土地，dust 成了关于必死的庄重意象，固定在 dust to dust 这一短语里。

intro.en: Dust is an Old English noun shared across the Germanic languages; the verb came later from the noun.
intro.cn: dust 是古英语名词，为多种日耳曼语言共有；动词是后来从名词变来的。

items.en: The word is sometimes connected with a root for smoke or fine vapour, but the evidence is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词有时被联系到一个表示「烟、细雾」的词根，但证据不确定。

items.en: The Germanic noun for dust is reconstructed in a form close to dustam, with relatives in several modern languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示「灰尘」的名词被重构为接近 dustam 的形式，在多种现代语言中都有亲属词。

items.en: Old English dust meant dust or powder, and it was already used in religious language about the body.
items.cn: 古英语 dust 意为「灰尘、粉末」，当时已用于关于身体的宗教语言。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun and added the verb sense of sprinkling powder or removing dust.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词，并增加「撒粉」与「掸灰」两个动词义。

items.en: The verb dust is recorded as both removing dust and applying powder, two opposite actions.
items.cn: 动词 dust 在十六世纪已有记录，既指去掉灰尘，也指撒上粉末，两个方向相反。

items.en: Dust storm, gold dust and dust to dust show the word spread across weather, trade and ritual.
items.cn: dust storm、gold dust 与 dust to dust 展示了这个词横跨天气、贸易与仪式。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dust; the near-meaning group separates dirt, powder and soot by what they are made of.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dust 构成的词形；近义组按构成区分 dirt、powder 与 soot。

entries.definition: Covered with or full of dust; dust plus -y.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「布满灰尘的」，由 dust 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A cloth or brush for removing dust; dust plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抹布、掸子」，由 dust 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A flat container used with a brush to collect dust and dirt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「簸箕」，与扫帚配合收集灰尘和脏物。

entries.definition: A container for household rubbish; dust plus bin, common in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾桶」，由 dust 加 bin 构成，常见于英式英语。

entries.definition: Unclean matter such as mud or grime; it is coarser and often wetter than dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「污物、泥垢」，比 dust 更粗、更常带湿。

entries.definition: A dry substance ground into fine particles; it may be clean and deliberate, unlike dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「粉末」，指磨成细颗粒的干燥物质，可能是干净且有意制成的。

entries.definition: Black powder left by smoke; a specific kind of dust from burning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烟灰、煤烟」，是燃烧留下的一种特定灰尘。

entries.definition: Small hard particles of stone or sand; coarser and heavier than dust.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「砂砾」，指石或沙的小硬颗粒，比 dust 更粗更重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the particles from the air to the shelf, then show the verb working in two opposite directions.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着颗粒从空气落到架子上，再展示动词两个相反的用法。

normal.en: Dust is matter small enough to float and settle: start with a sunbeam full of specks.
normal.cn: dust 是小到能漂浮、能落下的物质：先从一道满是细点的阳光开始。

normal.en: The verb dust can mean remove dust or add powder, so the object tells you the direction.
normal.cn: 动词 dust 既可指去掉灰尘，也可指撒上粉末，看宾语就知道方向。

normal.en: Dusty, duster and dustpan all keep the same particles in view.
normal.cn: dusty、duster 与 dustpan 都围着同样的颗粒。

normal.en: A dust storm is a whole sky turned into a cloud of particles.
normal.cn: dust storm 是一整片天空都变成颗粒的云。

normal.en: Dust to dust is the solemn phrase for the body returning to the ground.
normal.cn: dust to dust 是身体回归土地的庄重短语。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow beam of light crossing a room, every speck suddenly visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一道穿过房间的窄光，每一粒微尘忽然都看得见。

abstract.en: The same specks settle on a shelf, then rise again as a cloud over a dry road.
abstract.cn: 同样的微粒落在架子上，又在干燥的路面上重新升成一团云。

abstract.en: Dust is matter at its smallest and most patient, waiting on every surface.
abstract.cn: dust 是物质最小、最有耐心的形态，等在每一个表面上。

examples.en: Dust covered every shelf in the old room.
examples.cn: 灰尘盖满了那间旧屋的每一层书架。

examples.en: She dusted the furniture before the guests arrived.
examples.cn: 客人到之前，她掸去了家具上的灰。

examples.en: A cloud of dust rose from the dry road.
examples.cn: 干燥的路面上扬起一团尘土。

dict_mnemonic.text: dust 是阳光里浮动的细颗粒：落在架上是灰，扬在空中是尘，擦掉是掸灰，撒上是撒粉。

root: 古英语 dust「灰尘、粉末」，为日耳曼语共有词，重构形式接近 dustam；中古英语增加「撒粉」与「掸灰」的动词义，十六世纪两种相反用法均有记录。更早的印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of dust all centre on fine particles: settled on a surface, lifted as a cloud, wiped away, sprinkled on, or returned to the ground.
sensesIntro.cn: dust 的五个义项都围绕细小颗粒：落在表面、扬成云、被擦掉、被撒上，或回归土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: specks of matter floating in a beam of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束光里浮动的微小颗粒。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: particles that settle on shelves, roads and windows.
branches.cn: 表面线：落在书架、道路和窗上的颗粒。

branches.en: THE AIR: the same particles lifted into a visible cloud.
branches.cn: 空气线：同样的颗粒被扬成一团看得见的云。

branches.en: THE HAND: the verb can take dust away or put powder on.
branches.cn: 手线：动词既能拿走灰尘，也能撒上粉末。

branches.en: TWO STATES: settled dust and flying dust are the same matter in different motion.
branches.cn: 两种状态：落定的灰与飞扬的尘是同一物质的不同运动。

branches.en: THE RITUAL: dust becomes a solemn image for the body and the ground.
branches.cn: 仪式线：dust 成为身体与土地的庄重意象。

intro.en: Dust is a native Germanic noun; English adds -y, -er, -ed, -ing and compounds such as dustpan and dustbin.
intro.cn: dust 是本族语日耳曼语名词；英语加 -y、-er、-ed、-ing，并构成 dustpan、dustbin 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; Latin pulvis, dust, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 pulvis（灰尘）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基础。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「布满灰尘的；土色的」
由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「抹布；掸子」
由本词与 pan 复合，义为「簸箕」

definition_zh: 责任；义务；职责；税；值班
definition_en: a moral or legal obligation, a task that belongs to a job, a tax on goods, or a period of work
core_image: 肩上压着一块木牌，上面写着「必须做」
scene: 夜班护士在交班时把记录本递过去，走廊的灯仍亮着。The nurse finished her duty at dawn and handed over the notes.
sceneCN: 这里 duty 是「值班」（第 4 个义项：一段时间内的工作班次）；句意是那名护士天亮时值完班，把记录本交了出去。

pos.zh: 名词：责任；义务；职责；税；值班

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「尽职的；孝顺的」
由 dutiful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「尽职地；恭顺地」
由本词与 free 复合，义为「免税的」

senses.title: A moral or legal obligation
senses.definition: something that a person must do because it is morally right or required by law
senses.definitionCN: 因为道德上正确或法律要求而必须做的事
senses.example: He felt a duty to tell the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得自己有责任说出真相。
senses.why: Duty began as what is owed, and an obligation is a debt that is not counted in money.
senses.whyCN: duty 最初指「所欠之物」，而义务就是一笔不用钱来计数的债。

senses.title: A task belonging to a job
senses.definition: a responsibility or task that comes with a particular position or role
senses.definitionCN: 伴随某个职位或角色而来的责任或任务
senses.example: The guard's duties include checking every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 保安的职责包括检查每一位来访者。
senses.why: A job assigns specific things that must be done, so the abstract debt becomes a concrete list of tasks.
senses.whyCN: 一份工作会指派必须完成的具体事项，于是抽象的「欠」变成一张具体的任务清单。

senses.title: A tax on goods
senses.definition: a tax paid on goods, especially goods brought into a country
senses.definitionCN: 对货物所征的税，尤指进口货物
senses.example: The government raised the duty on cigarettes.
senses.exampleCN: 政府提高了香烟的税。
senses.why: A payment owed to the state for goods follows the same debt image, so duty also names a customs charge.
senses.whyCN: 因货物而欠国家的款项沿用同一个债务意象，所以 duty 也指海关征收的税。

senses.title: A period of work
senses.definition: a period during which someone is working, especially in a hospital, the army or a hotel
senses.definitionCN: 某人正在工作的一段时间，尤指医院、军队或酒店中的班次
senses.example: The nurse finished her duty at dawn and handed over the notes.
senses.exampleCN: 那名护士天亮时值完班，把记录本交了出去。
senses.why: The time when one is on duty is the time one owes to the job, so the obligation is measured out in shifts.
senses.whyCN: 一个人 on duty 的时间就是欠给工作的时间，于是义务被按班次量了出来。

intro.en: Duty comes from Old French deu, the past participle of devoir, to owe, and devoir goes back to Latin debere.
intro.cn: duty 来自古法语 deu，即 devoir（欠）的过去分词，而 devoir 又可追溯到拉丁语 debere。

items.en: Latin debere meant to owe or to be under an obligation, and it also produced debt and debit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 debere 意为「欠」或「负有义务」，还生出 debt 与 debit。

items.en: The past participle debitum meant something owed, and from it came the noun for a debt.
items.cn: 过去分词 debitum 意为「所欠之物」，由此产生表示债务的名词。

items.en: The verb devoir meant to owe or to be obliged, and its participle deu meant owed or fitting.
items.cn: 动词 devoir 意为「欠、应当」，其分词 deu 意为「所欠的、应有的」。

items.en: The noun deute named what is owed, including both moral obligations and payments.
items.cn: 名词 deute 指所欠之物，既包括道德义务，也包括应付款项。

items.en: Middle English dute carried the senses of obligation, service and a customary payment.
items.cn: 中古英语 dute 兼具「义务、服务、惯常应缴款项」几层意思。

items.en: The tax sense and the shift sense settled alongside the moral sense, giving the word its present range.
items.cn: 税与班次两个义项与道德义并存固定下来，形成今天这个词的义域。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on duty; the near-meaning group separates obligation, responsibility, task and tax by what is owed.
note.cn: 形近组收由 duty 构成的词形；近义组按所欠之物区分 obligation、responsibility、task 与 tax。

entries.definition: Doing what duty requires; formed from duty with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「尽职的、孝顺的」，由 duty 加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: In a manner that fulfils duty; dutiful plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「尽职地、恭顺地」，由 dutiful 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Exempt from the tax called duty; duty plus free.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「免税的」，由 duty 加 free 构成。

entries.definition: Owed or expected; both due and duty descend from the same French participle.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「应付的、预定的」，与 duty 同出同一个法语分词。

entries.definition: A moral or legal requirement; more formal and more binding than duty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「义务、责任」，比 duty 更正式、约束力更强。

entries.definition: The state of being in charge of something and answerable for it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「责任、负责」，指对某事负有掌管与交代之责。

entries.definition: A piece of work to be done; concrete, and without the moral weight of duty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「任务」，具体而不带 duty 的道德分量。

entries.definition: A tax on imports or exports; a technical trade word for the tax sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「关税」，是 duty 税义在贸易领域的专业说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the French participle for owed and then spread it across moral duty, job tasks, taxes and shifts.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从法语中表示「所欠」的分词出发，再把它铺到道德责任、工作职责、税与班次上。

normal.en: Duty and due share one origin: what is owed.
normal.cn: duty 与 due 同源，核心都是「所欠之物」。

normal.en: A moral duty is a debt no one can pay for you.
normal.cn: 道德上的 duty 是一笔别人替你还不了的债。

normal.en: A job turns duty into a list: duties are the tasks written into the role.
normal.cn: 工作把 duty 变成一张清单：duties 就是写进职位里的任务。

normal.en: A customs duty is money owed to the state for goods.
normal.cn: customs duty 就是因为货物而欠国家的钱。

normal.en: On duty and off duty measure the debt in hours.
normal.cn: on duty 与 off duty 用小时来计量这笔债。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden sign tied to a pair of shoulders, reading: must be done.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木牌绑在一副肩膀上，上面写着：必须做。

abstract.en: The same sign can be a law, a job description, a customs form or a hospital rota.
abstract.cn: 同一块牌子可以是一条法律、一份职位说明、一张海关单或一张医院排班表。

abstract.en: Duty is everything owed, whether to conscience, to an employer, to a state or to a ward.
abstract.cn: duty 是所有欠下的东西，无论欠的是良心、雇主、国家还是一个病房。

examples.en: He felt a duty to tell the truth.
examples.cn: 他觉得自己有责任说出真相。

examples.en: The guard's duties include checking every visitor.
examples.cn: 保安的职责包括检查每一位来访者。

examples.en: The nurse finished her duty at dawn.
examples.cn: 那名护士天亮时值完班。

dict_mnemonic.text: due 是「应付的」，duty 就是应付的那一份：对良心是责任，对工作是职责，对货物是税。

root: 经由古法语 deu（devoir 的过去分词，意为「所欠的、应有的」）来自拉丁语 debere「欠、负有义务」，与 due、debt、debit 同源。中古英语 dute 起兼有责任、服务与应缴款项诸义，后来固定为今天的四个主要义项。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of duty all name something owed: to conscience, to a job, to the state, or to a shift.
sensesIntro.cn: duty 的四个义项都在命名某种「欠」：欠良心的、欠工作的、欠国家的，或欠一个班次的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden sign tied to a pair of shoulders, reading must be done.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木牌绑在肩膀上，写着「必须做」。

branches.en: THE CONSCIENCE: a debt that is moral or legal rather than financial.
branches.cn: 良心线：一笔道德或法律上的债，而非金钱之债。

branches.en: THE JOB: the abstract debt becomes a written list of tasks.
branches.cn: 工作线：抽象的债变成一张写好的任务清单。

branches.en: THE BORDER: money owed to the state for goods crossing it.
branches.cn: 边境线：货物过境时欠国家的钱。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the debt measured out in working hours and shifts.
branches.cn: 时钟线：用工作小时和班次来量这笔债。

branches.en: ONE BIND: conscience, job and shift are three ways of saying what one owes.
branches.cn: 同一种约束：良心、工作与班次，是「欠」的三种说法。

intro.en: Duty is a French-Latin noun; English adds -ful, -ly and the compound -free.
intro.cn: duty 是源自法语的拉丁系名词；英语加 -ful、-ly，并构成 -free 复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin debere and debitum are recorded, and the French branch devoir, deu and deute is also well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 debere 与 debitum 均有记录，法语一支的 devoir、deu、deute 也有充分书证。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基础。

items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是最深层的来源。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun from the participle of debere
